questions.question: What are Core Web Vitals? Explain LCP, INP, and CLS.
questions.title: Core Web Vitals Explained — LCP, INP (replacing FID), CLS
questions.direct_answer:
What are Core Web Vitals? Explain LCP, INP, and CLS.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), INP (Interaction to Next Paint, replaced FID in March 2024), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift); targets and measurement.

**Classic weak answer:** Still citing FID — Google replaced FID with INP in March 2024; INP measures overall responsiveness, not just first input.

**Senior finish:** Give the thresholds (LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1), tools (CrUX, PageSpeed Insights, Web Vitals JS library), and how each affects SEO.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Core Web Vitals Explained — LCP, INP (replacing FID), CLS** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are Core Web Vitals? Explain LCP, INP, and CLS.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), INP (Interaction to Next Paint, replaced FID in March 2024), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift); targets and measurement**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still citing FID — Google replaced FID with INP in March 2024; INP measures overall responsiveness, not just first input**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Give the thresholds (LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1), tools (CrUX, PageSpeed Insights, Web Vitals JS library), and how each affects SEO**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), INP (Interaction to Next Paint, replaced FID in March 2024), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift); targets and measurement
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.

questions.question: How do you improve LCP, CLS, and INP on a web page?
questions.title: How to Improve LCP, INP & CLS — Optimization Techniques
questions.direct_answer:
How do you improve LCP, CLS, and INP on a web page?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** LCP: preload hero image, compress/lazy, defer non-critical JS; INP: break long tasks, use scheduler.yield, code-split; CLS: reserve space, size images, avoid injected content.

**Classic weak answer:** Trying to fix LCP with caching headers alone — the server response may be fast but the LCP element may be a late-loaded image; prioritize the correct asset.

**Senior finish:** Mention fetchpriority="high", Priority Hints, and the scheduler.yield API (2024) for breaking long tasks.

interviewer_intent.testing: LCP: preload hero image, compress/lazy, defer non-critical JS; INP: break long tasks, use scheduler.yield, code-split; CLS: reserve space, size images, avoid injected content
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Trying to fix LCP with caching headers alone — the server response may be fast but the LCP element may be a late-loaded image; prioritize the correct asset
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention fetchpriority="high", Priority Hints, and the scheduler.yield API (2024) for breaking long tasks
